- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75) — model tends to overreact and peak too early; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 72, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: if sentiment is rising but price hasn’t yet reacted, delay forecast peak by 1–3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is falling, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
